claims.text: For UWA coursework assessments, AI tools may only be used where the Unit Coordinator explicitly permits them; permitted use must be cited, referenced, and clearly acknowledged.

evidence.quote: For all coursework students AI tools may only be used in an assessment where it is explicitly permitted by your Unit Coordinator. Where it is permitted, you must always cite and reference your uses of it and provide clear acknowledgement of how AI was used.
evidence.title: Using ChatGPT and other AI tools in your assessments - askUWA

claims.text: UWA student assessment guidance describes three AI-use tiers that lecturers may apply to assessment tasks: Tier 1 no AI, Tier 2 AI assistance or collaboration, and Tier 3 fully embedded AI.

evidence.quote: AI Tiers that may be applied to assessment tasks by your lecturer | TIER 1: No AI | TIER 2: AI assistance or collaboration | TIER 3: Full Embedded AI
evidence.title: AI use in assessments
evidence.location: AI Tiers that may be applied to assessment tasks by your lecturer

claims.text: UWA askUWA guidance says limited AI editorial tools may be used for broad editorial assistance in a student's own writing, and the student remains responsible for judging whether suggestions are accurate and appropriate.

evidence.quote: Under UWA's Academic Integrity policy, you are permitted to limited use of AI tools for broad editorial assistance in your writing. This means that you can use spelling, grammar and style checkers for basic feedback on your own written work.
evidence.title: Use of AI tools for editorial assistance - askUWA

claims.text: UWA's 2026 student AI guide says students should not enter personal data or information into public AI systems.

evidence.quote: Students at UWA should not input any personal data or information into any public AI systems (such as ChatGPT, Google Gemini, and other similar systems).
evidence.title: Using Artificial Intelligence Tools at UWA: A Guide for Students

claims.text: UWA’s student AI guide expanded its privacy guidance to clarify that students must not input UWA staff intellectual property (lecture slides, handouts, unit reading material) into public AI systems.

evidence.quote: It is also important that you do not input any intellectual property or copyright material that is not your own, including the intellectual property of UWA or its staff – such as lecture slides, handouts, and unit reading material – as it is not yours to distribute.
evidence.title: Using Artificial Intelligence Tools at UWA: A Guide for Students

claims.text: UWA Library ethical guidance says users should never upload the University's intellectual property into a generative AI tool unless explicitly instructed to do so.

evidence.quote: You should never upload any of the University's intellectual property into a generative AI tool unless you are explicitly instructed to do so.
evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI): Ethical Considerations

claims.text: UWA has blocked DeepSeek services on UWA-managed devices and networks because of concerns about the safety and security of data shared with DeepSeek's online services.

evidence.quote: The University of Western Australia (UWA) has blocked access to DeepSeek services on all UWA-managed devices and networks. This decision follows directives from the Western Australian Government and the Department of Home Affairs, due to concerns about the safety and security of data shared with DeepSeek's online services.
evidence.title: Use of DeepSeek at UWA - askUWA

claims.text: UWA’s 2026 student AI guide now states that UWA staff and students must not use DeepSeek in any way, that UWA has blocked DeepSeek on University-managed networks and devices, and that students should avoid using DeepSeek on their personal devices.

evidence.quote: Additionally, not all AI platforms are safe to use. The Department of Home Affairs has raised concerns on the safety and security of data shared with the AI tool DeepSeek. As such, UWA staff and students must not use DeepSeek in any way. UWA has blocked the use of DeepSeek on all University-managed networks and devices, and students should avoid using DeepSeek on their personal devices.
evidence.title: Using Artificial Intelligence Tools at UWA: A Guide for Students

claims.text: UWA research-writing guidance states that AI and other machine-learning language models cannot be authors, and authors should transparently disclose when and how they used them.

evidence.quote: AI and other machine learning language models cannot be authors. Authors should be transparent when AI and other machine learning language models are used and provide information about how they were used.
evidence.title: Guidance on the use of AI and LLM in research writing
evidence.location: Guidance on the use of AI and LLM in research writing

claims.text: UWA research-writing guidance says authors are responsible for ensuring inputs to AI tools are suitable for uploading and processing and that use complies with copyright, privacy, ethics, data-sensitivity policies, and legislation.

evidence.quote: Authors are responsible for ensuring that all input into AI tools is suitable for uploading and processing and any use is compliant with copyright, privacy, ethics, and data sensitivity policies and legislation.
evidence.title: Guidance on the use of AI and LLM in research writing
evidence.location: Guidance on the use of AI and LLM in research writing
